issue: Must a party raise an objection in the district court to preserve a claim, or may an appellate court review a claim never presented below with de novo review under Fed. R. Crim. P. 51(a)?

sides.position: Claims never presented to the district court may be reviewed de novo because Rule 51(a) makes a postruling exception unnecessary. The court rejects this approach as contrary to the text of Rule 51 and to Supreme Court precedent.
Under Rules 51(b) and 52(b), a party must inform the court of its objection, and an unpreserved claim is reviewed only for plain error.
cases: United States v. Stapleton, No. 25-2201 (7th Cir. 2026)

this_court: Unpreserved claims are reviewed only for plain error under Rule 52(b); the court abandons its prior de novo review of claims never presented below.
quote: They are also in considerable tension with Supreme Court precedent and have created a lopsided circuit split.
cite: United States v. Jermaine Stapleton, No. 25-2201 (7th Cir. 2026)
